stages.title: Chapter 1-4 story
stages.note: The spine you cannot miss. Play it, but treat every chapter break as a deadline for whatever strand is still open.

stages.title: The finale
stages.note: The last mission. Everything in stages 2 through 8 has to be finished before you start it.

stages.title: Front-loaded missions
stages.note: Single-mission story and heist trophies that arrive while the plot runs. Unmissable, listed so the roadmap reads in narrative order.

stages.title: 100% completion
stages.note: The long gold. Track it from the in-game checklist rather than from this page.

stages.title: Activities & skill gates
stages.note: Stunts, ranges, races, meditation, arcade cabinets: the breadth of the state. Grind-friendly and never missable.

stages.title: Stranger strands
stages.note: Companion and stranger lines. These are the ones that expire: close each strand inside the chapter that opens it.

stages.title: Collectibles & coverage
stages.note: Card sets, WAiNK spots, vehicles, map fog. Route them district by district instead of criss-crossing the state.

stages.title: Heists & robberies
stages.note: Banks, trucks, shops, gangs. The escape counts as part of every requirement here.

stages.title: Economy & decisions
stages.note: Money loops, property and the hidden decision trophies. Last, because they want cash and a save file.

stages.title: The platinum
stages.note: The receipt: it arrives when the other fifty-four do.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum is a receipt rather than a task: it unlocks the moment the fifty-fourth other trophy lands and cannot be chased directly. Build the run around the two long golds, story completion and 100%, because they set the pace for everything else. The real risk is an abandoned stranger strand rather than any fight, so audit the missables before every chapter break.
trophies.why: No objective of its own: the platinum simply totals the other fifty-four.
steps: Unlock the other 54 trophies.
The platinum pops with the last one, wherever it happens.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Gone Fishing arrives early on the story chain, which makes it the cheapest trophy in the set. Follow the markers, watch the scene that closes the mission rather than skipping it, and the award lands on the results screen. Nothing in the mission branches, so there is no way to come out of it empty-handed.
trophies.why: An opening story mission with a single route and no optional objective.
steps: Play the story mission Gone Fishing.
Finish the last objective and let the results screen appear.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Chapter 1 is credited when its epilogue finishes, not when the last headline mission does. Keep playing the short follow-up jobs that appear after the main arc resolves, and confirm the chapter counter in the pause menu has rolled over. That same transition is where Leonida's missable clock starts, so it is worth noting which save you crossed it on.
trophies.why: Easy to earn, but the chapter's end quietly starts closing the map's first missables.
steps: Complete every Chapter 1 mission, epilogue included.
Let the chapter transition play out.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Chapter 2 widens the map: new districts, new strand markers, and most of the content that can later expire. Push the chapter's mission chain to its close while opening, not necessarily finishing, every new marker you see. The trophy wants only the mission set, so the discipline is not letting the plot outrun your notes.
trophies.why: Story progress only, but it unlocks the strands that the plot later takes away.
steps: Complete every Chapter 2 mission.
Bank the trophy as the chapter closes.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: By Chapter 3 free roam is rich enough to swallow whole evenings, so treat the main chain as the job and the map as the reward. Clear the chapter's missions, including the story jobs that feel optional because they sit off the main line, and check your open strands before the closing mission. The trophy follows the transition automatically.
trophies.why: Automatic on the chapter break, which is also where unfinished strands start dying.
steps: Complete every Chapter 3 mission.
The trophy pops on the chapter transition.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Chapter 4 runs straight into the ending, which makes it a last audit rather than a place to explore. Before the final chapter mission, walk the roadmap: every companion line closed, every one-time social beat done, every choice trophy you wanted already banked. Then cross the boundary, because the ending follows immediately.
trophies.why: A free trophy if the audit happens first, an expensive one if it does not.
steps: Complete every Chapter 4 mission.
Cross the boundary only once the missable list is clean.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The final mission is a gold for the milestone, not for the difficulty. Keep a manual save before starting so an unused branch stays reachable, then play through the epilogue without quitting, because the completion flag is written at the end of it. Skipping the closing scenes is the one habit that can finish the story without paying out.
trophies.why: The story's last mission: the fight is the map you leave behind, not the shootout.
steps: Close every missable strand and decision first.
Play the final mission and the epilogue to the credits.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Breakfast Run appears while the cast is still being introduced, so it needs no preparation at all. Play the objectives in order and let the closing scene run; the award is written when the mission settles, not when the shooting stops. There is no alternate outcome to worry about.
trophies.why: An early mission with no conditions beyond finishing it.
steps: Play the story mission Breakfast Run.
Let the mission-complete screen appear.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: The Cartel Heist is story-gated, so it cannot be started early from free roam and it rewards patience with the main chain. Complete the prep the story hands you, then run the job through the escape; stopping after the score does not count. The trophy is written on the job-complete screen.
trophies.why: A story heist where the getaway is part of the requirement.
steps: Finish the story missions that unlock the heist.
Run it to the end, escape included.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Child's Play sits mid-chain and asks for nothing clever. Finish the mission including whatever confrontation closes it, and let the post-mission scene play out before you quit or reload. Restarting for a cleaner run buys nothing here.
trophies.why: Mid-story content with no performance condition attached.
steps: Play the story mission Child's Play.
Finish it and let the scene after the last objective play.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Headliners is a set piece that unlocks once its predecessors are cleared, and it is all spectacle. Follow the objectives, stay in the fight through the last sequence, and do not quit out during the finale. The trophy lands on the completion banner.
trophies.why: A main-chain spectacle: reach the end and it is yours.
steps: Play the story mission Headliners.
Stay with the final sequence to the end.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: VCIA Takedown unlocks at the airport beat of the story. Work the whole objective chain, including the section where the mission hands you a vehicle, and avoid reloading a checkpoint after the final objective resolves. The award is tied to completion, so the epilogue is part of the job.
trophies.why: An airport mission whose only trap is quitting before the last objective settles.
steps: Play the story mission VCIA Takedown.
Complete the full chain without reloading at the end.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Operation Savage Glory is late-story content and stays locked until its prerequisites are done. Use the cover the level gives you, follow the objectives, and let the closing scenes run rather than skipping. There is no missable window inside the mission, so reaching the end is the whole requirement.
trophies.why: Late-story spectacle with nothing optional inside it.
steps: Unlock Operation Savage Glory by advancing the story.
Play it to the end.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Work from the in-game completion checklist and treat its categories as the source of truth, because the trophy reads that list and nothing else. Route collectibles and activities district by district so travel time stops being the cost, and reopen the checklist whenever you think a category is done. The final percent is nearly always one straggler, and no part of it needs another player.
trophies.why: The long gold: a checklist where the last two percent is a missed straggler.
steps: Open the in-game checklist and note every category under its maximum.
Clear them one at a time, routed by district.
Finish with whichever category the checklist still shows short.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Confirm which stunt type actually moves the counter before you commit, then build a loop of jumps in one region and land them cleanly. Repeating a jump already banked adds nothing, so keep a tally as you go. Two hundred and fifty is a patience test: a boring reliable route beats a flashy one you fail twice an hour.
trophies.why: Volume over skill: 250 counted stunts with no shortcut.
steps: Check which stunt type the counter accepts.
Work region by region, landing each jump cleanly.
Stop at 250 counted completions.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: The trophy counts distinct activity types, so read the in-game list first and note how many categories it actually contains. Try one of each as you find them and tick them off, because two similar pastimes are not necessarily two types. The award lands on the last new type you try, whatever the score.
trophies.why: Breadth, not repetition: one attempt at every category the list names.
steps: Read the activity list and count the types.
Try one of each type, ticking them off.
The trophy pops on the last new type.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: List the Shooting Range challenges and treat each as a small puzzle with a fixed solution. Gold usually hinges on the weapon the challenge was built around and on not wasting the first seconds, so learn the target order instead of spraying. One silver blocks the trophy, which means replaying the weakest challenge is always better than moving on.
trophies.why: A genuine skill gate where a single silver holds the trophy hostage.
steps: List every Shooting Range challenge.
Earn gold on each, retrying with the intended weapon.
The trophy pops on the last gold.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: The trophy counts venues, not wins, so mark every Top Fun location before you start flying. Drone courses reward clean lines and early braking, and a practice lap costs nothing. Win once per venue; repeat wins at the same course do not move the counter.
trophies.why: A location count: the same course twice is worth nothing.
steps: List every Top Fun location on the activity map.
Win a race at each venue.
The trophy pops at the last location.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Different is the word that matters: twenty wins around one circuit will not do it. Open the race list, note the events you have never won, and match the car to each discipline. Most races are decided at the first braking point, so take a learning lap before racing for the win.
trophies.why: Twenty distinct victories, where repetition is the expensive mistake.
steps: List the race events and mark the unwon ones.
Win twenty distinct races.
The trophy pops on the twentieth.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Cal's fishing contest comes out of his stranger strand, so start that line and follow it until he offers the challenge. Fish the marked deep water and let the line settle instead of reeling constantly; one catch heavier than his wins, and a loss costs only a retry. Finish it in the chapter that opens the strand, because the whole line can close.
trophies.why: A retryable patience contest that only expires with Cal's strand.
steps: Start Cal's strand and accept the fishing challenge.
Land a catch heavier than his.
The trophy pops on the win.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Any cabinet will do, since the requirement is one finished game rather than a high score. Stay on the machine until the end screen — walking away resets the run — and expect two or three attempts while you learn the pattern. The trophy pops on completion.
trophies.why: Cheap: one short pattern-based game played to its end screen.
steps: Find an arcade cabinet.
Play one game through to its end screen without leaving.
The trophy pops on completion.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Andy's companion strand is exactly the kind of content the story erases when it advances. Start the marker as soon as it appears and run the missions back to back, because some steps only trigger once the previous one has fully closed. The trophy is on the final mission of the line, so a half-finished strand is worth nothing.
trophies.why: A companion strand whose only difficulty is finishing it inside its chapter.
steps: Start Andy's strand when its marker appears.
Play every mission in the line.
The trophy pops on the strand's final mission.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Kenton's line opens in a set chapter and should be closed inside it. Run the missions consecutively where the game allows, and if the next marker stalls, pass time in-world with sleep or the phone rather than leaving the area. The award sits on the strand's last mission, and missing it means a fresh playthrough.
trophies.why: Missable strand content where delay, not difficulty, loses the trophy.
steps: Start Kenton's strand.
Complete the strand without leaving the chapter.
The trophy pops on its final mission.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Billy's strand is short, which makes it easy to postpone and easy to lose. Pick up the first job the moment the marker shows and clear each step as it appears. Never start a new chapter with one of his jobs outstanding, because the window closes with the story.
trophies.why: A short strand with a hard window: starting it in time is the whole task.
steps: Start Billy's strand as soon as it appears.
Complete every mission in it.
The trophy pops on the last one.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Eight completed strands is bookkeeping: eight missions from eight strangers will not satisfy it. Keep a list of every strand you open and mark it done only when its final job is finished. Short strands are the efficient targets, and longer companion lines can run in parallel.
trophies.why: Eight whole strands: an accounting problem rather than a skill check.
steps: Collect stranger markers as they appear.
Finish eight whole strands, tracking which are closed.
The trophy pops on the eighth.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Randy's strand is missable, so timing is the entire difficulty. Open it in the chapter where it appears and finish each job before taking a main-story mission that could push the chapter forward. The jobs are sequential, so sampling them out of order gains nothing.
trophies.why: A short missable strand where urgency is the only obstacle.
steps: Start Randy's strand.
Run it to its final mission.
The trophy pops on that mission.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Tyrone's line is another companion strand with a soft gate between missions. Take the marker when it appears, finish each job as offered, and skip time in-game if the next needs a day to trigger. Leaving it open across a chapter break is how players lose it.
trophies.why: Missable strand content with a time gate between its missions.
steps: Start Tyrone's strand.
Complete each job as it is offered.
The trophy pops at the end of the line.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Open the activity list and work from the meditation spots it names rather than scanning the horizon for something spiritual. Each location needs a full meditation: hold the input until the prompt completes, because a quick visit does not register. Nothing here can be missed, so it is a good quiet-session checklist.
trophies.why: A sightseeing checklist with no fail state anywhere in it.
steps: Get the meditation spot list from the activity map.
Meditate fully at each location.
The trophy pops at the last spot.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Bret's request names one specific animal, so read the brief before you leave. Track with the hunting sense instead of driving around hoping, and take a clean shot so the carcass still qualifies. The trophy pops on the kill, and because the request belongs to a strand, take it when it appears rather than saving it for later.
trophies.why: A single named animal whose strand window is the only thing that can close it.
steps: Take Bret's hunting request.
Track the named animal and kill it cleanly.
The trophy pops on the kill.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Each card set has a fixed list, and the final card is usually bought rather than found. Finish one set at a time: note the gaps, then close them with shops, vendors and packs. Two complete sets plus a near-miss third earns nothing, because the counter reads full sets only.
trophies.why: Collection luck plus shop money: three whole sets, last card usually bought.
steps: List the card sets and their counts.
Complete one set at a time, buying stragglers.
The trophy pops on the third completed set.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: WAiNK is location-based, so work district by district with the activity map open and tick each spot as you go. The counter wants distinct locations, so repeat visits are wasted time. Clear the districts you would otherwise skip early, because the last handful always hide there.
trophies.why: A hundred locations: a routing grind with no skill anywhere in it.
steps: Map which districts hold WAiNK spots.
WAiNK each one, district by district, marking them off.
The trophy pops at the hundredth.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Challenges appear while you are busy with something else, so the real skill is saying yes instead of driving past the prompt. Fold the fifty into collectible and activity runs rather than a dedicated session, and keep your own tally because free roam does not always surface the count.
trophies.why: Fifty opportunistic completions; the trap is ignoring the prompt.
steps: Accept challenges as they appear during other content.
Complete fifty of them.
The trophy pops on the fiftieth.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Set this one up deliberately instead of waiting for it to happen: bring the partner, raise the level to four stars, then break line of sight and let it decay all the way down without dying or being arrested. Tunnels, parking garages and storm drains are the dependable places to vanish.
trophies.why: Needs a partner and a clean four-star escape, and it expires with the story.
steps: Raise a four-star wanted level with the partner in the car.
Break line of sight and let the level decay to zero without dying.
The trophy pops when the level clears.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Choose three shops within a short drive of each other before you start, because the wanted level must survive the whole streak. Rob the first, keep the police live, and run straight to the second and third without shaking them. Fighting is optional and usually counterproductive: the unbroken run is the requirement.
trophies.why: A routing test: three shops robbed while the heat never drops.
steps: Pick three shops close enough to reach while wanted.
Rob the first, then the second and third without losing the level.
The trophy pops on the third robbery.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: A vehicle counts when you drive or inspect it, so variety beats ownership. Log the models at dealerships and garages, swap cars during missions instead of staying loyal to one favourite, and keep the list by class so a resprayed sedan is not counted twice.
trophies.why: A hundred distinct vehicles, dealerships included.
steps: Drive and inspect a wide spread of vehicles.
Visit dealerships and garages to register their stock.
The trophy pops at the hundredth.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Find a fight with at least five enemies and let them cluster before you trigger Combat Focus. Activate with all five in view and take them down in one continuous flow: reloading or losing sight of one usually ends the chain. Gang operations and story firefights are the natural places to try.
trophies.why: One clean Combat Focus with five enemies clustered, nothing more.
steps: Find a fight with five or more enemies grouped up.
Activate Combat Focus with all five in view.
Drop all five before the meter empties.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Get airside at VCIA without using the scheduled departure route, either by boarding a parked aircraft or by driving through the service access. Once airborne and past the airport boundary the departure registers, so pick a heading away from the runway before you lift off. The trophy pops in the air, not on the ground.
trophies.why: Cheap and funny: a stolen plane out of VCIA with a wanted level as the receipt.
steps: Reach the VCIA apron or a parked aircraft.
Take off without a scheduled departure.
The trophy pops once airborne and clear.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The Rhino comes from the military content, so reach that part of the story or activity before worrying about anything else. Then read the description literally: it is a joke about one specific act performed while driving the tank. With the vehicle in hand the trophy takes seconds.
trophies.why: A joke trophy gated only by getting the Rhino.
steps: Get the Rhino from the military content.
Perform the act the description alludes to while driving it.
The trophy pops on the trigger.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Case the store before you go in: note the back entrance, the safe, and where the staff stand. Enter quietly, take the contents without touching an alarm, and leave the way you came. Any alarm voids the attempt, so restart the robbery rather than improvising a rescue.
trophies.why: The only stealth trophy in the set: one alarm voids the whole attempt.
steps: Case the store's entrances and the safe.
Take the contents without raising an alarm.
The trophy pops when the robbery completes undetected.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Identify all five vaults first and treat each as its own small heist with a planned exit. The trophy requires a clean escape after every robbery, not just the score, so space the jobs out while heat is high. A failed getaway only costs that attempt.
trophies.why: Five clean vault escapes, where planning the exit matters more than the robbery.
steps: Identify the five bank vaults.
Rob each and escape cleanly.
The trophy pops on the fifth escape.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Armored trucks run predictable routes, so wait at a junction instead of chasing one down the highway. Block it, take the cargo, and break the escort before it regroups. One clean job is all the trophy wants, which makes a quiet stretch of road better than a busy one.
trophies.why: One armored truck and a clean getaway; route knowledge beats firepower.
steps: Intercept an armored truck on its route.
Take the cargo and shake the pursuit.
The trophy pops once you are clear.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Open the map, find the fogged regions, and travel through each until the fog lifts. Flying covers the far corners fast, but driving fills the road-level gaps the map actually counts. Save the islands and the state's edges for last, since they are the easiest to overlook.
trophies.why: Map coverage: the fog hides the last regions, not any difficulty.
steps: Find the regions still fogged on the map.
Drive or fly through each until the fog clears.
The trophy pops on the last region.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: The game tracks each gang as a separate target, so identify who runs what before you start hitting operations. Rob one per gang and keep a list, because hitting the same gang twice does nothing. A quiet approach is optional but keeps the getaway short.
trophies.why: One operation per gang; repeating a gang is the trap.
steps: Identify each gang and the operation it runs.
Rob one operation per gang, tracking progress.
The trophy pops on the last gang's operation.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: The venue matters: it is the specific bar with the view on Ocean Beach, not any kiosk on the sand. Order a cocktail and finish it, because leaving with the glass half full does not register. The beat is tied to the story and the venue can close later in the plot, so drink while it is open.
trophies.why: A one-time social beat at one bar, missable once the story moves on.
steps: Find the Ocean Beach bar with the view.
Order and finish a cocktail there.
The trophy pops on the drink.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive a vehicle into a showroom, then leave by smashing through the frontage rather than reversing politely out of the door. The game wants the dramatic exit, so line the window up and commit. The trophy does not care about the wanted level that follows.
trophies.why: Cheap spectacle: drive in, smash out, no skill required.
steps: Drive a vehicle into a showroom.
Smash out through the frontage.
The trophy pops on the break-out.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Go to the Kolt & Associates alley and bowl a complete game through to the final frame. The trophy checks the finished game, not the score, so do not quit halfway. Bring the companion the game offers if it does, since the lane is a social activity.
trophies.why: A full bowling game: cheap, social, and easy to abandon one frame early.
steps: Go to the Kolt & Associates bowling alley.
Bowl a full game to the last frame.
The trophy pops on the final frame.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: This is a decision trophy tied to a partnership beat, so it cannot be chased from the map. Play the story, make the choice the scene presents, and keep a manual save beforehand because the other branch may not award it. Once the choice is made the award appears on its own.
trophies.why: A hidden decision trophy: the branch you take decides whether it exists.
steps: Play the story to the partnership beat.
Make the choice, with a manual save kept beforehand.
The trophy pops on the beat.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Either branch of the decision satisfies this trophy, so the only way to lose it is to back out of the scene. Play to the moment, make the call, and let the consequences land. Keep a manual save before the mission if you are farming the other decision trophies too.
trophies.why: Either branch counts; the only cost is refusing to choose.
steps: Play to the decision the trophy is tied to.
Make the choice — either branch counts.
The trophy pops at the decision.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: The description is literal: the trophy is attached to a deliberate second attempt. Play the story to that beat and retry the way the scene intends instead of reloading to dodge the failure. Keep a save before the sequence, because a clean first attempt can skip the trigger entirely.
trophies.why: Tied to a second attempt that a clean reload quietly skips.
steps: Play to the repeat attempt the trophy names.
Take the second attempt as the scene intends.
The trophy pops on that attempt.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: A hidden trophy attached to a story moment rather than a task, so the only route is to play until you reach it. Let the scene play out fully instead of skipping the sequence it names. Because it is hidden, the list will not tell you what it is until it appears.
trophies.why: A hidden story beat with no task attached: reach it or do not.
steps: Play the story.
Let the moment it names play out in full.
The trophy pops on the moment.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Get a vehicle and a melee weapon, then connect with a pedestrian while the car is still rolling. Timing is the whole challenge: the swing has to land from a moving vehicle, not a standstill. A quiet street with a slow approach beats heavy traffic, where the target moves unpredictably.
trophies.why: A timing gag: the melee hit must land from a moving car.
steps: Get a vehicle and a melee weapon.
Land the melee hit from the moving vehicle.
The trophy pops on the hit.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Marked Bills come from robberies and jobs, and they only count once passed through your contacts. Launder in batches instead of hoarding, because the trophy measures the total through the contact rather than the cash in your pocket. Repeat the loop whenever it is available and keep a running note.
trophies.why: A money loop, not a skill test: $250,000 through your contacts.
steps: Collect Marked Bills from robberies and jobs.
Launder them through your contacts repeatedly.
The trophy pops at $250,000 laundered in total.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Every purchase at every shop counts, which makes this a trophy you earn by playing normally with a spending habit. Buy useful things as you go instead of saving for one grand splash, and spread purchases across shops so you are never waiting on stock. Clothing, weapons and vehicle upgrades all add up.
trophies.why: Cumulative shopping where every purchase counts toward $100,000.
steps: Buy from shops of every kind as you play.
Spread purchases so no single shop's stock gates you.
The trophy pops past $100,000 cumulative.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: List every garage property on the market before buying anything, because the trophy checks the whole set and the last one is easy to overlook. Garages are expensive, so fund them from heists and the money loops, and buy the cheap ones early to spread the cost across the run.
trophies.why: The most expensive checklist item: every garage, funded by heists.
steps: List every garage property for sale.
Buy them all, cheapest first.
The trophy pops on the last purchase.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Open the Scooter Bros app in the in-game phone and register ten vehicles. Anything you own counts, so a full garage clears the requirement in one sitting. The app is easy to forget exists, which is the only real obstacle here.
trophies.why: Ten free app registrations; the obstacle is remembering the app exists.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app in the in-game phone.
Register ten vehicles you own.
The trophy pops on the tenth.
